input.question: How was airline security done prior to the TSA?
input.ground_truth: I'm not sure about all these people claiming there was no security at all pre-9/11, there most certainly was (there wouldn't be scenes spoofing it in the Airplane! movies if there was no security...). Hijackings and bombings were certainly a thing before 2001. I recall a school trip in 1989 when one of my classmates made a joke about having a gun when going through security and getting a very stern talking to from the Airport Security person. There was little in the way of centralized authority, however, most airports contracted out their own security force, so details would be different from airport to airport, and would often be not too much above Mall Cops. Typically there would be a metal detector you would go through, possibly an x-ray for carryons. However, there was no checking to see if you had a valid boarding pass. If I was dropping someone off or picking someone up, I could go right to the gate myself, even though I wasn't flying that day.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How was airline security done prior to the TSA?

Answer:

response.prediction: Before the TSA, people who wanted to fly on airplanes didn’t have to go through the same kind of checks we see today. There were no special lines or machines like X-ray scanners for your bag or body. People could just walk up to the airport, show their ticket, and go straight to the plane. Sometimes, there was a very simple check, like someone looking at your ticket or maybe asking to see your ID, but that’s about it. They didn’t check your bags for things that could be dangerous, and you didn’t have to take off your shoes or put your liquids in a small bottle. It was much easier and faster, but also less safe.
